items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: And then Al Pitrelli added some guitar stuff and that all of a sudden became a hit.

ctx.x: Yeah. So anyway, we started writing and we wrote a musical called “Romanov, When Kings Must Whisper,” and a couple of other things. And meantime Paul had this idea for doing something with “Carol of the Bells,” and he had a guitar intro for “God Rest Ye Merry Gentlemen.” And we worked on that together for a while, and then Christmas Eve Sarajevo 12/24” came out of that. You know we wrote some original music too, and combined it with the well-known carols and created that piece. And then Al Pitrelli added some…

song starts out with the cello solo playing “God Rest Ye Merry Gentlemen” with a guitar ostinato. Anyway, so he read the whole story, and it was like boy-girl on each side, and hear the music and come together, and it’s just like part of the healing process for peace. And he read the whole thing and then they played the song, and then he started talking about it. So it got like ten minutes of airtime on the song. And then of course the phones lit up there too, so they started playing it regularly. And it spread…
